ss3diags2 user guide

Diagnostics, stock status and fleet impacts for Stock Synthesis, with FLR inputs and outputs

Henning Winker, Massimiliano Cardinale, Laurence T. Kell, Iago Mosqueira

13 November 2026

1 ss3diags2: Stock Synthesis diagnostics in FLR and ggplot2

ss3diags2 is the successor of ss3diags (Winker et al.; Carvalho et al. 2021). It reads the output of Stock Synthesis (SS3; Methot and Wetzel 2013) as returned by r4ss::SS_output() and provides:

  • Observations as FLR objects. Catch, discards and length and age compositions as FLQuants by fleet, indices as FLIndices, life-history parameters as FLPar, all with the SS3 structure in the FLQuant dimensions (sex as unit, season, area). The same objects are the inputs of JABBA3 and FLicc.
  • Residual diagnostics. One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals for compositions (Trijoulet et al. 2023), runs tests, joint residual plots, retrospective analysis (Mohn’s rho) and hindcast cross-validation (MASE), as in the diagnostics cookbook (Carvalho et al. 2021).
  • Stock status with uncertainty. FLStockR objects with reference points, maximum likelihood estimates or draws from a multivariate lognormal (MVLN) approximation of the SS3 Hessian (Kell et al. 2023; Walter and Winker 2020), trajectories, Kobe plots and the production function.
  • Fishing mortality and impacts. F-at-age by fleet, partial F by fleet, gear or area, F and stock by area, and the partial impact of fleets on the spawning stock (Wang et al. 2009), from the SS3 report without re-running SS3.
  • data.table and ggplot2. Long tables with FLQuant dimension columns (len/age, year, unit, season, area, iter, data) that convert directly to FLR; no dplyr.

How ss3diags functions map to ss3diags2:

ss3diags ss3diags2
SSplotRunstest(), SSrunstest() ss3_runs(), ss3plot_runs() (indices, mean length, mean age)
SSplotJABBAres(), SSrmse() ss3plot_jres()
SSplotRetro(), SShcbias() ss3_retro(), ss3_mohn(), ss3plot_retro()
SSplotHCxval(), SSmase() ss3_hindcast(), ss3plot_hcxval()
SSdeltaMVLN(), SSplotKobe() ss3mvln(), ss3stk(), ss3plot_trj(), ss3plot_kobe(), ss3plot()
SSsettingsBratioF() reference point basis in ss3stk() (same logic, benchmark labels)
SSplot_eqcurves() ss3_eqcurve(), ss3_spm(), ss3plot_production()
SSgetComps() ss3_lencomp(), ss3_agecomp()
(Pearson residuals in r4ss) ss3_resid() (OSA), ss3plot_resid()

1.1 About this guide

Part I (sections 3-9) goes through the diagnostics of an assessment, from the data to the prediction skill, with checks at each step (what to look at, what is a red flag, what to do about it), following the diagnostics cookbook. Part II (sections 10-14) covers stock status and its uncertainty, the timing of F and SSB in Kobe plots, the production function, season-, sex- and area-structured models (F by area, stock by area, partial impact of fleets) and the FLR outputs. Section 15 summarises the checks and the functions.

The examples ship with the package:

Data Model Used for
ss3simple simulated two-sex model, one fishery and two surveys (r4ss “simple_small”; the example of the PIFSC ss3diags) quick start, data, residuals
ss3sma, retro.sma, aspm.sma North Atlantic shortfin mako (cookbook) runs tests, retrospective, status, Kobe
ss3phk, retro.phk, aspm.phk Pacific hake (cookbook) Dirichlet-multinomial OSA residuals, hindcast
pra.27.3a4a.rds northern shrimp, four seasons, hermaphrodite, two areas, six area-specific fleets structured models, F by area, impact

2 Installation

2.1 Required

ss3diags2 needs FLCore, data.table and ggplot2. Install from r-universe (the same repositories provide the FLR packages):

repos <- c(
  hw   = "https://henning-winker.r-universe.dev",
  flr  = "https://flr.r-universe.dev",
  CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
)
install.packages("ss3diags2", repos = repos)

Or the development version from GitHub:

remotes::install_github("Henning-Winker/ss3diags2")

2.2 Optional

Package Needed for Install
r4ss reading SS3 output (SS_output(), SSgetoutput(), SSsummarize()) install.packages("r4ss")
mvtnorm, MASS MVLN draws (ss3mvln(), output = "iters") and Kobe contours install.packages(c("mvtnorm", "MASS"))
patchwork the summary page ss3plot() and side-by-side plots install.packages("patchwork")
ss3diags comparing with the original functions remotes::install_github("jabbamodel/ss3diags")
JABBA3, FLicc, FLRef the models fed by the extracted inputs see the packages

2.3 Check the installation

library(ss3diags2)
library(ggplot2)
packageVersion("ss3diags2")
#> [1] '0.1.0.9000'
opt <- c("r4ss", "mvtnorm", "MASS", "patchwork", "ss3diags")
data.frame(package = opt, installed = vapply(opt, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE), row.names = NULL)
#>     package installed
#> 1      r4ss      TRUE
#> 2   mvtnorm      TRUE
#> 3      MASS      TRUE
#> 4 patchwork      TRUE
#> 5  ss3diags      TRUE

3 Quick start

An SS3 run is read with r4ss::SS_output(); the report list is the input of ss3diags2. The simulated ss3simple model ships with the package (its SS3 files are in system.file("extdata", "simple_small", package = "r4ss")):

ss3rep <- r4ss::SS_output("path/to/run", verbose = FALSE, printstats = FALSE)
data(ss3simple)
ss3_fleets(ss3simple)
#>    fleet    name   type  area catch_units survey_units ncatch
#>    <int>  <char> <char> <int>      <char>       <char>  <int>
#> 1:     1 FISHERY  catch     1     biomass      biomass     13
#> 2:     2 SURVEY1 survey     1        <NA>      biomass      0
#> 3:     3 SURVEY2 survey     1        <NA>      numbers      0
#>    nindex  nlen  nage
#>     <int> <int> <int>
#> 1:      0    12    12
#> 2:      4     4     4
#> 3:     12     0     0

3.1 Quick output: ss3plot()

ss3plot() is the one-page summary of an assessment, as the JABBA3 summary plot:

  • top row: SSB (with the observed indices scaled to SSB as points), F and catch, with the reference points (unfished in blue, targets in green, Bpa orange, Blim red);
  • middle row: SSB and F relative to their targets, and the Kobe plot with the uncertainty of the terminal year;
  • bottom row: the stock-recruitment curve, the recruitment deviations with 95% intervals and the production phase plot (catch against SSB on the Kobe colours, with the equilibrium yield curve).
ss3plot(ss3simple, iters = 500)

Uncertainty comes from MVLN draws of the SS3 Hessian. The targets are named after the benchmark SS3 used (here B40: 40% of unfished SSB, with Fmsy; section [Stock status]).

3.2 Stock status as FLR

stk <- ss3stk(ss3simple)                     # FLStockR at the MLE, reference points in @refpts
stk@refpts
#> An object of class "FLPar"
#> params
#>     Ftgt     Btgt      MSY       B0       R0 
#> 1.98e-01 2.19e+04 4.96e+03 5.48e+04 7.54e+03 
#> units:  NA
ss3plot_trj(stk)

4 Data: observations as FLR objects

The extraction functions return the observations of an SS3 run, and with what = "exp" the model fit, as FLR objects. Each fleet is one element of an FLQuants; the SS3 structure goes into the FLQuant dimensions:

SS3 FLQuant dimension note
length or age bin len / age data bins; empty bins of sampled compositions are filled with 0
year year
sex (data Sexes 1-3) unit F, M; combined-sex data stay unique
season season seasons stay seasons
area area the area of the fleet
partition 0/1/2 fleet name fleet.all, fleet.discard, fleet.retained 
ct  <- ss3_catch(ss3simple)                  # FLQuants: catch by fleet
idx <- ss3_indices(ss3simple)                # FLIndices of FLIndexBiomass: index, index.var (input SE)
lfd <- ss3_lencomp(ss3simple)                # FLQuants: length compositions by fleet, sex as unit
afd <- ss3_agecomp(ss3simple)

ss3plot_comps(lfd,type="annual",year=2015:2022)

Every extractor also returns the long data.table (long = TRUE), with the FLQuant dimension columns:

head(ss3_lencomp(ss3simple, long = TRUE), 3)
#>    fleet    name partname   len  year   unit season   area   iter
#>    <int>  <char>   <char> <int> <int> <char> <char> <char> <char>
#> 1:     1 FISHERY  FISHERY    26  2011      F    all unique      1
#> 2:     1 FISHERY  FISHERY    28  2011      F    all unique      1
#> 3:     1 FISHERY  FISHERY    30  2011      F    all unique      1
#>           data  part ageerr month         obs        exp   pearson
#>          <num> <int>  <int> <int>       <num>      <num>     <num>

#> 3: 0.004975125     0      0     7 9.95025e-05 0.00146581 -0.252530
#>    nsamp_adj nsamp_in    effN   used nsamp           n      nexp

#> 1:        50       50 43.6548    yes    50 0.004975125 0.0835860

4.1 Data overview

ss3plot_data(catch = ct, indices = idx, lencomp = lfd, agecomp = afd)

4.2 Compositions

ss3plot_comps() shows compositions pooled over years, by year, as bubbles (only the years with data) or as mean length or age over time, split by unit, season or area (by =), for a subset of fleets and units:

ss3plot_comps(afd, type = "bubble", by = "unit")

ss3plot_comps(lfd, type = "mean", by = "unit")

4.3 Inputs for JABBA3 and FLicc

ss2jabba3() returns catch in weight by fleet and annual indices with input SEs, the inputs of JABBA3; ss2flicc() returns length compositions by gear on common bins, with ss3_lhpar(), the inputs of FLicc.

j <- ss2jabba3(ss3simple)
names(j)
#> [1] "catch"       "indices"     "fleets"      "catch.total"

Check 1: data. Look for contrast in the indices (a one-way trip gives little information on productivity), conflicting trends between indices, and compositions with few samples or gaps. ss3plot_nsamp() shows the input and effective sample sizes.

5 Life history and growth

ss3_lhpar() returns an FLPar of growth, maturity, length-weight and natural mortality, with a unit dimension when the model has two sexes; this is the lhpar of FLicc. Growth other than von Bertalanffy is approximated by a von Bertalanffy curve fitted to the SS3 growth at the end year.

lh <- ss3_lhpar(ss3simple)
lh
#> An object of class "FLPar"
#>            unit
#> params      F         M        
#>   linf       7.33e+01  7.33e+01
#>   k          1.42e-01  1.42e-01
#>   t0        -2.62e+00 -2.62e+00
#>   L50        5.50e+01  5.50e+01
#>   mat.slope -2.50e-01 -2.50e-01
#>   a          2.44e-06  2.44e-06
#>   b          3.35e+00  3.35e+00
#>   M          1.00e-01  1.00e-01
#>   CVmin      1.00e-01  1.00e-01
#>   CVmax      1.00e-01  1.00e-01
#>   A1         0.00e+00  0.00e+00
#>   A2         2.00e+01  2.00e+01
#>   L1         2.28e+01  2.28e+01
#>   L2         7.03e+01  7.03e+01
#> units:  NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA
ss3plot_growth(ss3simple, lfd = lfd)

Ridge plots show the length compositions by year, observed (filled) and expected (lines), with the growth curves by sex tracking cohorts through the bins:

ss3plot_ridges(lfd, fit = ss3_lencomp(ss3simple, what = "exp"), type = "both", fleets = "SURVEY1", lhpar = lh)

6 Check 2: model fits

ss3plot_indices(idx, fit = ss3_indices(ss3simple, what = "exp"))

ss3plot_comps(lfd, fit = ss3_lencomp(ss3simple, what = "exp"), by = "unit")

Check 2: fits. The fitted index should follow the trend of each index; systematic misfits at the start or end of a series, or an index fitted only where it agrees with another, point to conflicts between data sources. Pooled compositions should be fitted without systematic misfit of the small or large bins.

7 Check 3: residual diagnostics

7.1 One-step-ahead residuals for compositions

Pearson residuals of multinomial compositions are correlated across bins (they must add up), so their patterns can mislead. One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals (Trijoulet et al. 2023) condition each bin on the bins before it; under a correct model they are independent N(0, 1). ss3_resid() computes them for the SS3 likelihood: multinomial with the adjusted sample size, or Dirichlet-multinomial with the precision implied by the SS3 effective sample size. Growth curves by sex (lhpar) track cohorts.

rl <- ss3_resid(ss3simple)                   # length; ss3_resid(ss3simple, "age") for ages
ss3plot_resid(rl, lhpar = lh)

ss3plot_resid(rl, type = "qq")

Pacific hake uses the Dirichlet-multinomial for its age compositions:

data(ss3phk)
ss3plot_resid(ss3_resid(ss3phk, "age"), cohorts = FALSE)

Reading OSA residuals. Bins are conditioned on the smaller bins: too few small fish gives negative residuals at small sizes and positive residuals at larger sizes. Diagonal patterns that follow the growth curves are year classes the model does not fit.

7.2 Runs tests and joint residuals

The runs test checks the log residuals of each index (or the mean length or age) for randomness; the 3-sigma limits come from the average moving range (Carvalho et al. 2021). North Atlantic shortfin mako:

data(ss3sma)
ss3_runs(ss3sma)
#>     index runs.p   test  sigma3.lo sigma3.hi
#>    <char>  <num> <char>      <num>     <num>
#> 1: CPUE_1  0.069 Passed -0.2605783 0.2605783
#> 2: CPUE_2  0.717 Passed -0.7630777 0.7630777
#> 3: CPUE_3  0.229 Passed -0.5033328 0.5033328
#> 4: CPUE_4  0.406 Passed -0.5868380 0.5868380
#> 5: CPUE_5  0.065 Passed -0.3369695 0.3369695
#> 6: CPUE_6  0.870 Passed -3.0226356 3.0226356
ss3plot_runs(ss3sma)

ss3plot_jres(ss3sma)

Check 3: residuals. Red flags: a failed runs test (p < 0.05), residuals outside the 3-sigma limits, trends in the joint residuals (lowess line), RMSE above 30%. Actions: look for conflicts between indices, changes in catchability, selectivity or growth; never drop data only to pass a test.

8 Check 4: retrospective analysis

Retrospective runs refit the model with the last years of data removed (peels; r4ss::retro()), read with r4ss::SSgetoutput() (and optionally r4ss::SSsummarize()). ss3_retro() turns them into FLStocks (one FLStockR per peel); ss3_mohn() gives Mohn’s rho and the forecast rho (the one-year-ahead projection of each peel against the reference run), as ss3diags::SShcbias().

data(retro.sma)
rt <- ss3_retro(retro.sma)
ss3_mohn(rt, c("SSB", "F"))
#>      quant     peel          rho       fcrho
#>     <char>   <char>        <num>       <num>
#>  1:    SSB     2014  0.020093362  0.02045794
#>  2:    SSB     2013  0.042894147  0.04379605
#>  3:    SSB     2012  0.063855565  0.06529724
#>  4:    SSB     2011  0.087619622  0.08975344
#>  5:    SSB     2010  0.083003822  0.08466103
#>  6:    SSB Combined  0.059493304  0.06079314
#>  7:      F     2014 -0.019624432 -0.02679539
#>  8:      F     2013 -0.002872149 -0.01684454
#>  9:      F     2012 -0.042739851 -0.06472934
#> 10:      F     2011 -0.085448219 -0.10706880
#> 11:      F     2010 -0.078531045 -0.10968634
#> 12:      F Combined -0.045843139 -0.06502488
ss3plot_retro(rt, type = c("SSB", "F"))

Check 4: retrospective. Mohn’s rho outside -0.15 to 0.20 (long-lived species; -0.22 to 0.30 for short-lived species; Hurtado-Ferro et al. 2015) is a red flag, as are forecasts outside the confidence interval of the reference run. Actions: look at recent data, time-varying catchability or selectivity.

9 Check 5: hindcast cross-validation

The hindcast compares the observations of the peeled years with their one-year-ahead predictions from the retrospective runs (Kell et al. 2016). The mean absolute scaled error (MASE) scales the prediction error by that of a naive random-walk forecast: MASE < 1 means the model predicts better than the naive forecast. ss3_hindcast() does indices, mean length and mean age, as ss3diags::SSmase().

data(retro.phk)
hc <- ss3_hindcast(retro.phk)
hc$mase
#>              index     MASE    MAE.PR  MAE.base MASE.adj n.eval
#>             <char>    <num>     <num>     <num>    <num>  <int>
#> 1: Acoustic_Survey 1.064745 0.3022749 0.2838943 1.064745      4
#> 2:           joint 1.064745 0.3022749 0.2838943 1.064745      4
ss3plot_hcxval(hc)

ss3plot_hcxval(ss3_hindcast(retro.sma))

Check 5: prediction skill. MASE > 1 for an index means the model has no prediction skill for it. With indices that vary little the naive error is small and MAE.base.adj (default 0.1) limits the scaling.

10 Stock status: FLStockR and MVLN

ss3stk() builds a simplified FLStockR (as FLRef::ss2FLStockR()): SSB, F, recruitment and catch, with the reference points in @refpts. output = "mle" gives the maximum likelihood estimates with their standard errors, output = "iters" draws from a multivariate lognormal (MVLN) approximation (ss3mvln()):

  • method = "joint" (default) draws SSB, recruitment and F of all years and the reference points from one MVLN with the full correlation matrix of the SS3 derived quantities (Kell et al. 2023; the ss3om::ssmvln() approach). Each draw is a coherent trajectory and the reference points have draws.
  • method = "annual" is the delta-MVLN of ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN() (Walter and Winker 2020; Winker et al. 2019), drawn year by year from the B ratio, F and the F reference.
stk <- ss3stk(ss3sma, output = "iters", iters = 1000, fwd = TRUE)
ss3plot_trj(stk)

SSdeltaMVLN understates the B-F correlation. For the example models the year-by-year delta-MVLN gives a correlation between B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy in the terminal year of -0.24 for shortfin mako (SS3 covariance: -0.86) and -0.26 for Pacific hake (-0.76), so its Kobe clouds are rounder than the estimated uncertainty. The joint method keeps the estimated correlation; use it for advice.

10.1 Which targets: the reference point basis

SS3 can report stock status relative to different benchmarks, set in starter.ss (the B ratio denominator and the F report basis) and forecast.ss (the benchmarks; the MSY option can be set to the F at a biomass target or at an SPR target). The SS3 labels of the derived quantities also changed between versions. ss3stk() works out the basis with the logic of ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN() and SSsettingsBratioF():

  1. B ratio: the SS3 Bratio of the end year is compared with SSB relative to SSB virgin, SSB_MSY and SSB_Btgt (or SSB at F0.1); the closest defines the B target.
  2. F basis: from F_std_basis (SS 3.30) or F_report_basis (3.24): absolute F, F/Fmsy, F/F at the B target, or F/F at the SPR target.
  3. F reference: MSY, unless the MSY benchmark is the B target benchmark (then the F at the B target) or the SPR benchmark (then the SPR F); Fref = overrides it.

The status values agree with SSdeltaMVLN() for all example models and for the SS3 benchmark options. The labels name the benchmark behind each target rather than the SS3 label, because “MSY” in SS3 output may be a proxy:

Basis B target F target Catch reference
MSY benchmark Bmsy Fmsy MSY
B ratio relative to B0, target fraction 40% B40 (from the F basis)
biomass target 40% (or MSY set to F(B40)) B40 F40 Y40 (yield at B40) when MSY is the proxy
SPR target 40% (or MSY set to F(SPR40)) Bspr40 Fspr40 Yspr40 when MSY is the proxy
F0.1 BF0.1 F0.1

The catch reference stays MSY when SS3 estimated MSY. The basis is stored in attr(stk, "basis"):

str(attr(ss3stk(ss3sma), "basis")[c("B", "F", "C", "bbasis", "fbasis")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ B     : chr "Bmsy"
#>  $ F     : chr "Fmsy"
#>  $ C     : chr "MSY"
#>  $ bbasis: chr "SSB/SSBMSY"
#>  $ fbasis: chr "(F)/(Fmsy)"
str(attr(ss3stk(ss3simple), "basis")[c("B", "F", "C", "bbasis", "fbasis")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ B     : chr "B40"
#>  $ F     : chr "Fmsy"
#>  $ C     : chr "MSY"
#>  $ bbasis: chr "SSB/SSB0"
#>  $ fbasis: chr "_abs_F"

10.2 Key quantities as FLQuants

q <- ss3_flqs(stk, c("SSB", "F", "B/Btgt", "F/Ftgt"))
names(q)
#> [1] "SSB"    "F"      "B/Btgt" "F/Ftgt"

11 Kobe plots and the timing of F and SSB

Critical for advice. SS3 reports SSB at spawning (typically at the start of the year), and F of year y acts during year y. The SSB that results from the fishing in year y is therefore SSB in year y + 1. The usual Kobe plot pairs F(y) with SSB(y): it shows the biomass the fishery in y started from, not the biomass it led to. When F is well above Fmsy, the stock status that follows from the current exploitation can be markedly worse than the plot of F(y) against SSB(y) suggests. Advice should state which convention is used and, when the two differ, show both.

ss3plot_kobe(lag = 1) plots F(y) against B/Btgt(y + 1). The uncertainty cloud then pairs F(Y) with B(Y + 1) within each draw, which needs draws linked across years: use method = "joint". Build the stock with fwd = TRUE so that SSB at the start of the year after the last assessment year (an SS3 forecast quantity) is available; F is used up to the end year only.

k0 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk) + ggtitle("lag = 0: F(y) against B(y)")
k1 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk, lag = 1) + ggtitle("lag = 1: F(y) against B(y + 1)")
patchwork::wrap_plots(k0, k1)

For North Atlantic shortfin mako the probability of being in the red quadrant (overfished and subject to overfishing) in 2015 is about 78% with F(2015) against SSB(2015) and about 93% with F(2015) against SSB(2016).

Before using the lagged plot for advice. SSB(y + 1) for the last assessment year is a one-year forecast: it depends on the SS3 forecast settings (forecast.ss) and, where recruits mature within a year, on the forecast recruitment. Kell et al. (2023) pair F and SSB both ways in their figures; the convention is not standardised, which is why it must be stated with the advice.

12 Production function and equilibrium

ss3_eqcurve() extracts the SS3 equilibrium yield curve and ss3_spm() fits a Pella-Tomlinson production function to it, as a surplus production model equivalent of the age-structured model (the “production function” of JABBA3), and checks it against the SS3 benchmarks.

sp <- ss3_spm(ss3sma)
sp
#> Pella-Tomlinson fit to the SS3 equilibrium curve (K free), R2 = 0.99988
#>         r         K         m       MSY      Bmsy     BmsyK 
#>    3.8890 1152.0000    2.2700 1035.0000  604.3000    0.5244 
#>      Hmsy 
#>    1.7130 
#> 
#> Check against SS3 benchmarks:
#>    quantity       SS3       SPM  rel.diff
#>      <char>     <num>     <num>     <num>
#> 1:      MSY 1041.5400 1035.1364 -0.006148
#> 2:     Bmsy  603.5820  604.3169  0.001218
#> 3:       B0 1158.0100 1152.3628 -0.004877
#> 4:  Bmsy/B0    0.5212    0.5244  0.006124
ss3plot_production(ss3stk(ss3sma))

ss3plot_production(ss3stk(ss3sma), type = "dyn")

Which unfished state? SS3 holds several: SSB_Virgin (start-year biology), SSB_unfished (benchmark years) and the dynamic B0 of each year. With time-varying weight-at-age or M (empirical wtatage, as for Pacific hake) these differ, and the equilibrium table can rest on yet another biology. ss3_spm() warns when its fit and the SS3 benchmarks differ by more than 5%.

13 Season-, sex- and area-structured models

The Stock Synthesis assessment of northern shrimp (Pandalus borealis) in Skagerrak and the Norwegian Deep (pra.27.3a4a, SS 3.30.22, 1970-2024) uses most of the structure SS3 offers: four seasons (spawning in season 1), two sexes with protandric hermaphroditism (born male, change to female), two areas (1: Skagerrak 3.a, 2: Norwegian Deep 4.a) with time-varying recruitment distribution, six area-specific fleets (Denmark, Norway, Sweden in each area) with retention and discards, and two surveys with sex-specific length compositions. F is reported as Fbar over ages 1-3 (Z - M) and the MSY benchmark is set to the F at B30%. The report and the SS3 input files ship with the package.

dir <- system.file("extdata", "pra.27.3a4a", package = "ss3diags2")
pra <- readRDS(file.path(dir, "pra.27.3a4a.rds"))
ss3_fleets(pra)
#>    fleet        name   type  area catch_units survey_units ncatch

13.1 Observations by season, sex and area

Because each fleet fishes in one area, the observations need no area split: the area is a property of the fleet.

ss3plot_catch(ss3_catch(pra), by = c("season", "area"))

lfp <- ss3_lencomp(pra)
ss3plot_comps(lfp, fit = ss3_lencomp(pra, what = "exp"), fleets = c("NORSURVEY3a", "NORSURVEY4a"), by = "unit")

ss3plot_resid(ss3_resid(pra, fleets = c("NORSURVEY3a", "NORSURVEY4a")), lhpar = ss3_lhpar(pra))

13.2 Selectivity, retention and the stock by area

ss3plot_sel(ss3_sel(pra), ret = ss3_sel(pra, "ret"))

ss3plot_byarea(ss3_byarea(pra))

13.3 Summary and status

The MSY benchmark is set to the F at B30%, so the targets are B30 and F30 and the catch reference is the yield at B30 (Y30):

ss3plot(pra, iters = 500, lag = 1)

13.4 F-at-age, partial F and F by area

ss3_fa() returns F-at-age by fleet with the full structure (age, year, unit, season, area); F-at-age is on an annual scale within each season, and annual = TRUE sums the seasons weighted by their duration.

fa <- ss3_fa(pra)
ss3plot_fa(fa)

Partial F splits the reported F (Fbar 1-3) among fleets, gears or countries by their catch in numbers over the F ages, so it adds up to F:

countries <- list(Denmark = c("DK3a", "DK4a"), Norway = c("NOR3a", "NOR4a"), Sweden = c("SWE3a", "SWE4a"))
ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra, groups = countries))

ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra), type = "line")

Two notions of F by area. The partial F by area (groups = "area", method = "catch") is each area’s share of the stock F and adds up to it. The F experienced by the fish in an area (method = "fbar", the Fbar of the fleets of that area) is the F of a stock by area; F’s of different areas do not add up to the stock F when the stock is spread over the areas.

ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra, groups = "area", method = "fbar"))

13.5 Stock by area

ss3stk(area = TRUE) returns FLStocks with the stock and one FLStockR per area: SSB, recruitment and catch by area, and the F experienced in each area. Area reference points are approximations: B0 and R0 are the unfished values of the area, the B target is scaled by the area’s share of B0 and the F target is that of the stock.

sa <- ss3stk(pra, area = TRUE)
ss3plot_trj(sa)

13.6 Partial impact of fleets

ss3_impact() follows Wang et al. (2009): SSB is projected without fishing and with the fleet groups added one by one, so the impact of a group is the SSB it removes, and all impacts add up to the dynamic B0 minus SSB. It runs on the SS3 report without re-running SS3: annual total mortality from the SS3 numbers at age (seasons, areas and sexes pooled), fishing mortality Z−MZ - M split among fleets by their catch at age, the SS3 spawning output at age and recruitment deviations, and each scenario starting from the initial equilibrium under the initial F of its fleets. The run with all fleets reproduces the SS3 SSB and the run without fishing the SS3 dynamic B0:

imp <- ss3_impact(pra, groups = countries)
imp
#> Partial impact (Wang et al. 2009), cumulative - groups: Denmark, Norway, Sweden 
#> max relative difference SS3 vs projected SSB (all fleets): 4.4e-16
#> max relative difference SS3 vs projected dynamic B0 (init = "equilibrium"): 1.6e-05
#> impact in 2024 :
#>      group    impact       prop
#>     <fctr>     <num>      <num>
#> 1: Denmark 15852.480 0.46196805
#> 2:  Norway 16201.220 0.47213092
#> 3:  Sweden  2261.401 0.06590103
ss3plot_impact(imp)

ss3plot_impact(imp, type = "prop")

Approximations. When fleets are removed, movement, sex change and the timing within the year stay at their fitted values. The order in which the groups are added matters for the share of each group when the stock-recruit relationship is not flat; type = "remove" gives the loss of SSB caused by each group with all others fishing.

14 FLR outputs

Output Function Class
catch, discards by fleet ss3_catch(), ss3_discards() FLQuants
indices ss3_indices() FLIndices (FLIndexBiomass)
length, age compositions ss3_lencomp(), ss3_agecomp() FLQuants
OSA / Pearson residuals ss3_resid() FLQuants
life history ss3_lhpar() FLPar (unit by sex)
selectivity, retention ss3_sel() FLQuants
F-at-age by fleet ss3_fa() FLQuants (age, year, unit, season, area)
partial F ss3_partialF() FLQuants (total F as attribute)
stock by area ss3_byarea(); ss3stk(area = TRUE) FLQuants; FLStocks
stock status ss3stk() FLStockR (@refpts)
retrospective peels ss3_retro() FLStocks
key quantities ss3_flqs() FLQuants
MVLN draws ss3mvln()$flqs, ss3_flqs(mvln) FLQuants with iterations

long2flq(), long2flqs() and flqs2long() convert between the long tables and FLR objects. The stock objects work with FLRef and ggplotFL:

library(ggplotFL)
plot(ss3_flqs(ss3stk(ss3sma), c("SSB", "F", "Catch")))

14.1 MVLN draws as FLQuants with iterations

ss3mvln() returns the draws as FLQuants with one iteration per draw ($flqs): SSB, F, recruitment, catch, B/Btgt and F/Ftgt, and B/B0 and Catch/MSY where the reference points are reported. ss3_flqs() selects quantities from it, and ss3plot_flqs() plots the median with 50% and 90% bands, with the ratio panels named after the benchmark and a few single draws (“worms”) if wanted:

mv <- ss3mvln(ss3sma, mc = 1000)              # joint MVLN draws

The year-by-year delta-MVLN draws (method = "annual") as FLQuants, for Pandalus with the B30 and F30 targets:

mp <- ss3mvln(pra, mc = 1000, method = "annual")
ss3plot_flqs(ss3_flqs(mp, c("SSB", "Rec", "B/Btgt", "F/Ftgt")))

The same FLQuants come from the stock with iterations, ss3_flqs(ss3stk(ss3sma, output = "iters")), and work with ggplotFL (plot(mv$flqs)).

15 Summary of checks and functions

# Check Red flag Action
1 data (ss3plot_data, ss3plot_nsamp) no contrast; conflicting indices; few samples sensitivity runs; data weighting
2 fits (ss3plot_indices, ss3plot_comps) systematic misfit conflicts between data; selectivity, catchability
3 residuals (ss3plot_resid, ss3plot_runs, ss3plot_jres) failed runs test; residuals outside 3 sigma; RMSE > 30% time-varying q, selectivity or growth
4 retrospective (ss3_mohn, ss3plot_retro) Mohn’s rho outside -0.15 to 0.20 (short-lived: -0.22 to 0.30) recent data; time-varying processes
5 hindcast (ss3_hindcast, ss3plot_hcxval) MASE > 1 index without prediction skill
6 status (ss3stk, ss3plot_kobe) Kobe lag changes the quadrant state the convention; show both
